					<div class="sm-article-body" itemprop="articleBody"><p>With a spot in the quarter-finals of the <a href="/football/concacaf-nations-league/fixtures.html" target="_blank">CONCACAF Nations League</a> still within reach, <a href="/football/honduras/" title="Honduras">Honduras</a> will welcome <a href="/football/jamaica/" title="Jamaica">Jamaica</a> to Estadio Nacional Chelato Ucles on Monday.</p><p>After three Group B fixtures, the Hondurans sit fourth with three points, losing 2-1 to Martinique last time out, as they trail the Reggae Boys by three points for second, with the latter blanking El Salvador 2-0.</p><hr class="divide"><h2>Match preview</h2><p>It is now or never for the Hondurans at the Nations League, a side that have thrown away two matches in the competition this season.</p><div class="akcelo-wrapper akcelo-adunit-12489">
    <div id="Sportsmole_Incontent_1"></div>
</div>

<p>Jose Francisco Molina’s men have led at one point in two of their three Nations League affairs so far, only to lose.</p><p>Honduras can snap a two-match losing run at home in this competition on Monday, conceding a combined five goals in those last two defeats.</p><p>A win could put La H into second place depending on goal difference, but a loss would see them relegated as they are tied on points with Martinique and El Salvador, the two teams below them who will face each other on matchday four.</p><p>The Central Americans have never finished a Nations League group phase with fewer than two wins, a record that is in jeopardy on Monday.</p><p>Los Catrachos are unbeaten in their last two meetings with the Jamaicans, posting successive clean sheets against them in this competition.</p><div class="akcelo-wrapper akcelo-adunit-12489">
    <div id="Sportsmole_Incontent_2"></div>
</div>
<script type="application/javascript">

<div><img data-img-id="148991" class="lazy" loading="lazy" src="https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/l_ni9C_ujl-PyV2wk7CA-KcvUA8=/640x480/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2Fandre-blake-684cc43daefa4379413020.jpg"><div class="sm-image-copyright">© Imago</div></div><p>Jamaica bounced back impressively from a matchday two defeat against Honduras (1-0), taking control after gaining an early man advantage versus El Salvador.</p><p>That was <a href="/people/rudolph-speid/" title="Rudolph Speid">Rudolph Speid</a>’s first away victory as their manager at this tournament which put his team in a strong position to make the last eight for a third successive occasion.</p><p>A win on Monday would guarantee they advance into the knockout phase, while that, combined with a Suriname defeat, would see them top the group.</p><p>In addition, maximum points on matchday four would also give them one more than they finished with in the opening stage of this competition in 2024-25 (eight).</p><p>On Sunday, they can extend their winning run away from home in the Nations League group phase to six matches, while they have never lost a League A outing as the visitors at this stage of the tournament.</p><p>At the same time, the Reggae Boyz can stretch their winning run against their upcoming opponents in Honduras to four matches, claiming a 2-1 triumph the last time they faced them at Estadio Nacional Chelato Ucles in 2024.</p><p class="bM8">Honduras CONCACAF Nations League form:</p><div class="full">

</div><hr class="divide"><h2>Team News</h2><div><img data-img-id="165581" class="lazy" loading="lazy" src="https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/B21A3LpI3iSZSpqJ9OhURm5J0ng=/640x480/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F09%2Fimago1078284716h-2-6abd770dee0f6364192151.jpg"><div class="sm-image-copyright">© Imago / IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire</div></div><p>The Hondurans could be missing Denil Maldonado due to a physical issue, while <a href="/people/david-ruiz/" title="David Ruiz">David Ruiz</a> and <a href="/people/jorge-alvarez/" title="Jorge Alvarez">Jorge Alvarez</a> will hope to get back into the lineup, having missed the last match after incurring some travel issues.</p><p>Erick Puerto gave them the early lead on matchday three after just eight minutes, the first for the national team for the striker who features in Belarus for BATE Borisov.</p><p>For Jamaica, <a href="/people/renaldo-cephas/" title="Renaldo Cephas">Renaldo Cephas</a> is doubtful because of a knock, while Rumarn Burrell is out through injury, as is Leon Bailey.</p><p>Javon East netted a brace in their matchday three triumph, while captain <a href="/people/andre-blake/" title="Andre Blake">Andre Blake</a> only had to make one stop for the clean sheet.</p><p><strong>Honduras possible starting lineup:</strong></p><p>Menjivar; Melendez, Sacaza, Vega, Rosales; Flores, Arriaga; Toro, Puerto, Arana; Rochez</p><p><strong>Jamaica possible starting lineup:</strong></p><p>Blake; Latibeaudiere, King, Freckleton; Campbell, Anderson, Clarke, Webster; J. East, Dixon; Cadamarteri</p><hr class="divide"><p class="sm_center"> </p><div><img data-img-id="76176" class="lazy custom-size" loading="lazy" data-img-sz="210x53" src="https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/aAWazEIN-TXYyGNUOzzmBClUe-g=/210x53/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2F20%2F33%2Fsm-words-green-background.png"></div><p> </p><h2 class="sm_center">We say: Honduras 1-2 Jamaica</h2><p>At this stage of the Nations League, the Jamaicans always seem to find the right solutions, and we believe they will have a psychological edge against a Honduran side struggling to finish matches strongly.</p><p>For data analysis of the most likely results, scorelines and more for this match <a href="/football/concacaf-nations-league/honduras-vs-jamaica_game_259446.html"> please click here</a>.</p><hr class="divide"><hr class="divide"><p> </p>

                } else {
                    window.open(shareUrls[network], '_blank', 'width=600,height=400');
                }
            }
